Marco Rose saluted the in-form Evanilson after the Brazilian scored for a sixth Premier League game in a row to lift Bournemouth up to fourth place with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest .
Evanilson’s brilliantly taken 19th-minute opener set his side on course for a club record ninth straight win in all competitions, while the defeat means Forest are only above the relegation places on goal difference having failed to build on the momentum of their 3-1 win against Manchester City before the international break.
Rose said: “We defend together as a team, and we attack together as a team, but the forward guys were excellent today. They did a great job scoring the goals and the other guys support them. Evanilson creates space, carries the ball, provides assists and now he scores goals as a No 9, really beautiful goals so I am happy.”
Both teams started the game on the front foot and Forest had the first sight of goal. Neco Williams nodded dangerously across the face of goal at the far post, but Liam Delap was beaten to the ball by home defender Antonio Silva.
Evanilson was denied by a brilliant last-ditch tackle from Forest centre-back Jair Cunha before Marcus Tavernier’s 20-yard curler was well saved by Matz Sels.
Bournemouth took the lead in the 19th minute. James Hill cushioned a header into the path of Evanilson, and the Brazilian took one touch before blasting a left-foot shot into the roof of the net.
Justin Kluivert almost doubled the home side’s lead with an effort from 20 yards which sailed narrowly over the crossbar. Evanilson then failed to keep his shot down after a long throw from Hill caused chaos in the Forest penalty area.
Oliver Glasner’s side had a penalty appeal waved away when Adam Smith blocked Williams’s effort into the arm of teammate Tyler Adams. But Kluivert did make it 2-0 on the stroke of half-time with a simple far-post finish after a superb run and cross from Tavernier.
Forest were much improved in the second half, adopting a more direct approach in a bid to find a way back into the game. Delap turned provider by whipping in a cross for Morgan Gibbs-White but the captain could not properly connect with his header.
• Bournemouth have won five successive games in the top-flight of English football for the first time. Only Arsenal (67, before Newcastle game) and Manchester City (60) have collected more Premier League points in 2026 than the Cherries (52 – W13 D13 L4).
• Bournemouth have won each of their last nine games in all competitions, their longest ever such run, overtaking two separate runs of eight in 1998-99 and 2012-13.
• Nottingham Forest failed to score in this game despite registering 2.14 expected goals, the highest xG tally by any team not to score in a Premier League match this season. Opta
James McAtee ballooned an effort over the bar as the visitors continued to misfire in front of goal. The substitute Chris Wood also miscued a header from a corner when he should have at least tested the underworked Bournemouth goalkeeper, Djordje Petrovic.
Bournemouth always looked a threat on the counter and Kluivert came close to his second and Bournemouth’s third when he stung the gloves of Sels from 18 yards out. Kluivert should also have been more clinical when he found himself within finishing range but unselfishly laid the ball off to Rayan and the chance went begging.
Glasner, whose side had 19 shots but only one on target, said: “Of course when you lose it’s always a tough 90 minutes, especially when you make too many mistakes like we did in the first half.
“The second goal straight before half-time was a little bit of a killer but credit to the lads in the second half for finding a filter back into the game. We had some good situations, but we couldn’t convert them.
“We are not able to score in this game, and this is what we have to look at and where we have to improve. We took too many touches, and were not so aggressive.”

Bournemouth continued their unstoppable form with a comfortable 2-0 victory against Nottingham Forest and created two bits of history in the process.
It was a club-record ninth successive win in all competitions and the first time they have won five in a row in the Premier League. They have kept seven clean sheets in those games as well - only conceding against Ipswich in the league - with 23 goals scored.
A large part of that has been down to the form of Evanilson, and the Brazilian did not disappoint. He struck first with a wonderful effort - set up by the deftest of headers from James Hill - to extend his scoring run to six straight Premier League games.
It was a simple but effective break for Bournemouth's second as Forest failed to follow up a big win against Manchester City before the international break.
Marcus Tavernier sped down the left-hand side, with only Justin Kluivert for support. That was all he needed, though, as his low cross was turned home by the Netherlands international.
Bournemouth drew a number of fine saves from Matz Sels in the second half, although perhaps the brightest moment was the return of Alex Scott from injury. It was his first Cherries appearance since September 20 and his first overall game since October 3, when he played for England against Croatia.
He was part of a triple change in the 69th minute and from then on, Forest had the better of the play. However, they did little with it and could only muster one shot on target, despite have just one fewer shot than the Cherries (18).
The win sends Bournemouth into the top four ahead of the remaining games this weekend. Nottingham Forest slip down into 17th and are outside the relegation spots on goal difference.

Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose: "Really good [performance], especially in the first half. We knew that it's going to be difficult against a tough opponent, quite compact, consistent in everything they do.
"It's hard to create chances, but we did it. We created chances, we scored goals and we were relentless. We defended our goal at the end... with a deserved win.
"We were good in box defending. We never struggled really, we suffered, but we never struggled. It's an important part and phase of the game as well."
On Bournemouth's second goal: "It was the right moment, but if you're 2-0 up at half-time, it's always difficult if the opponent changed something and they did it.
"They brought [on] two new players, new energy and you could get in problems if you don't use the right approach for the second half, but we did it. We were ready and that's why it was a top performance. We enjoy this win, but Thursday [against Celta Vigo] we have to prove it again."
On Bournemouth's impressive defensive record: "This is the foundation for everything that we are - a hard-working team out of possession and that we do it together.
"Then we win balls, we score simple goals out of ball wins. And on the other side, we score goals from set-pieces. So we are unpredictable - and that's good."
"We need to be more physical. We're struggling with the physicality, the intensity and the power these teams have. We have to improve because then we can stay in all these games.
"We had the same amount of shots most of the time, but this is the pattern and we never scored. We always conceded from a mistake and we all know especially in defence, you have to avoid mistakes because the Premier League is ruthless.
"In the attack again we try, but you also have to be ruthless because otherwise the Premier League will punish you.
"It was a very intense game from both sides, many long balls, many duels, many second balls. We have to accept that Bournemouth was a little bit better in these situations and that's why they won.
"First goal we lose the ball, second goal we lose the ball. We were well-organised behind the ball and I don't know why, but it happened and then we open the middle and this is where they score the goal.
"Especially the second goal straight before half-time, such an easy goal to give away. That hurts and then you can't win in the Premier League.
"For me today [Saturday] it was not the efficiency, it was that we made too many easy mistakes and Bournemouth took them."

Luca Williams-Barnett's performance in his first Premier League start was that good it had two of his Tottenham team-mates labelling him "incredible".
The 18-year-old winger delivered the opener with his first senior goal and then played a pivotal role in Dominic Solanke's second as Spurs comfortably beat Ipswich 2-0 at home .
Yet what might be a sign of the excitement about his potential was manager Roberto de Zerbi calmly explaining that "his talent is bigger than this performance".
The Tottenham boss obviously believes this is just the beginning for the talented teenager.
Williams-Barnett became the youngest Spurs player to score in the Premier League since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007.
They would be pretty impressive footsteps to follow in if he was to get close to the player Bale once was for the north London club.
But for the slightest of touches on his fizzed ball across the area from Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton before Solanke turned home, Williams-Barnett would have become the second-youngest player ever to both score and assist in a Premier League game, aged just 18 years and 51 days old.
Only Michael Owen, who did it at 17 years and 364 days for Liverpool in 1997, would have done it at a younger age.
"He's incredible, honestly," Solanke told Final Score. "We get to see him every day in training so we know what a player he is - the confidence he has, the ability he has.
"The world got to see it today, which is great for him. His confidence and ability is amazing. He'll help us a lot."
Luca Williams-Barnett scored on his first start in the Premier League
Williams-Barnett was born in Luton and played for his hometown club before moving to Spurs at the age of 10.
The teenager has been generating excitement with his performances for the club's underage teams for some time.
Back in the 2023-24 season, he played for Tottenham 's Under-18s aged just 15 and in the following campaign he scored the Under-18 Premier League goal of the season against Leicester having become renowned for fine long-range strikes.
Williams-Barnett has been around Tottenham 's first-team since the 2024-25 campaign as he was on the bench for three Europa League games and a Premier League match but his debut came last season as a substitute in a Carabao Cup game against Doncaster Rovers under previous boss Thomas Frank.
Last December, he scored five goals in a Under-19 UEFA Youth League game against Slavia Prague.
Williams-Barnett featured in the EFL Cup as a substitute in a 5-1 victory over Charlton in August before coming off the bench against Crystal Palace and Leeds in the Premier League.
Yet it was still a bold choice from De Zerbi to make Williams-Barnett the club's sixth youngest starter in Premier League history given Spurs were coming into this game on the back of a defeat by Leeds United which checked a recent upturn in form.
However, the Spurs boss was rewarded with a man-of-the-match worthy display.
His goal was one of endeavour as he brushed in front of Ipswich defender Abdoul Ouattara to reach Pedro Porro's cross and become the club's youngest scorer on their Premier League full debut.
Throughout the game, he was looking for the ball constantly and not afraid to run with it and try to make things happen.
"Obviously I am so happy for him, every day in the training session he shows his quality," Tottenham defender Destiny Udogie told BBC Match of the Day.
"Honestly he's just an incredible football player. I hope he keeps doing what he's doing."
The winger was unfortunate not to get the assist but the goal does not happen without his powerful cross.
The England youth international was not afraid to take on a shot and his four attempts were all on target while he had a passing accuracy of 77.4% among his 44 touches.
Only Solanke took on more shots in the game with four of his five on target.
"To see him come in and do that on his first Premier League start is crazy," added Solanke.
"He's a great person and is obviously still young, you know what young boys are like.
"But he's very dedicated and so brave on the ball which is great, in his position I think you need that."
Roberto De Zerbi post-match interview - Tottenham Hotspur v Ipswich Town
Williams-Barnett was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute which brought a standing ovation from the crowd but, with the Brazilian then being forced off later on with an injury, there may be more opportunities in the coming weeks.
Obviously there will be more excitement about the talented teenager now which De Zerbi will have to manage and he has picked midfielder James Maddison as a good mentor for the attacker.
"He's played very well, but his talent is bigger than this performance," the Spurs boss told BBC Match of the Day.
"It was the first game and I am very happy, I am very delighted for his performance, but he is a big, big, big talent.
"The management of the younger talented players is different because you can't take risks to lose their enthusiasm and their positive mentality. But I think Tottenham 's dressing room now is a good environment for him.
"I put [James] Maddison to play very close to him to speak the same language but also to help him and put him in the best conditions to play. To play with freedom, to play with his qualities because his qualities are very big.
"He has to work hard but also he has to keep the passion to keep the love of football."

Report and free match highlights as teenager Luca Williams-Barnett stars in Tottenham's 2-0 home win over Ipswich; the 18-year-old made Spurs history with his 15th-minute opener; England U19 international then involved in Dominic Solanke's second-half goal as Ipswich go five without a win
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett scored on his first Tottenham start to make history in Spurs’ 2-0 home win over Ipswich.
The 18-year-old bundled home the opener at the back post in the 15th minute to become the youngest Spurs player to score on his first Premier League start for the club.
The Spurs academy graduate then turned provider in the second half as he terrorised the Ipswich defence from his left-wing position to tee up Dominic Solanke with a low cross for a simple 51st-minute finish.
But Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton's diversion into Solanke's path meant Williams-Barnett was not credited with the assist officially.
It meant Williams-Barnett, at the age of 18 years 51 days, just missed out on becoming the second-youngest player to both score and assist in a Premier League game (Michael Owen in December 1997 at 17y 364d).
The teenager was substituted in the 64th minute to a standing ovation and rapturous cheers from the Spurs fans, who had serenaded Williams-Barnett with Harry Kane's 'He's one of our own' chant - raising hopes that the club may have unearthed a new academy hero.
The England U19 international's dazzling display inspired Tottenham to a third consecutive home league victory for the first time in two years, lifting Roberto De Zerbi's side to ninth and within three points of the top five.
But the Italian had to watch the deserved win from the stands as he served a one-game touchline ban after receiving three yellow cards this season.
His opposite number Gary O'Neil, meanwhile, saw his side's winless run extend to five games as Ipswich rarely threatened the home side to leave the Tractor Boys in 16th and just two points above the relegation zone.
Spurs head coach De Zerbi believes Williams-Barnett is a "special player" and is a similar talent to Barcelona teenage sensation Lamine Yamal.
De Zerbi said at his post-match press conference: "He is a special player. I'm not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think.
"He played very well. He's lucky because he's playing in a top club with top team-mates.
"Yesterday evening, when I gave the first 11 to the players, I said, 'remember your debut and help the kid tomorrow, because he's one of us and if he plays well, we have more chances to win the game'.
"He's very young but at the same time he's a mature guy. He understands the right behaviour to keep in the dressing room - and he's older than his age."
He added: "The first day I spoke with Luca, I asked him two things: to play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom and to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are really the attackers even if they are Ballon d'Or or now the wingers or any players with talent, they have to work on the pitch."
Then asked whether Williams-Barnett is a special talent like PSG's Ballon d'Or winner Dembele and Spain's World Cup-winner Lamine Yamal, De Zerbi replied: "Yes, I think so.
"One of the best things in my career as a player, I've seen today on the bus from the training ground to the stadium. He was very close to me on the bus, and while we were coming to the stadium, he was watching Ronaldinho and Hazard on YouTube.
"I thought he was a special guy because, one hour and 30 minutes before your debut in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, [Eden] Hazard, Neymar, all this type of talent.
"Football is magic, no? The qualities, okay, but also the passion - you understand football, how football can be."
After a handful of encouraging substitute displays this season, the 18-year-old was deservedly handed his first Spurs start - and boy did he take it.
He dazzled on the left wing to become the youngest Spurs player to score in the Premier League since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007 (18y 47d).
Bale would go on to become a Spurs great, and there will be optimism that Williams-Barnett can do the same.
Every time he touched the ball in the win over Ipswich, there was real excitement at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, which has been in short supply in recent times.
He was a constant threat to the Ipswich defence as defenders backed off him, which exactly led to Solanke's goal.
The stats back up his impressive performance - he had the most touches in the opposition box (8) and big chances (2) of any player, while no player had more than his four shots on target.
For all of Spurs' big summer spending, their new hero looks to be from within.

Not since the emergence of a certain Harry Kane has there been this much excitement about a player from Tottenham’s academy. On his first senior start, Luca Williams-Barnett showed just why as the 18-year-old became their youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 before teeing up Dominic Solanke with a mesmerising and match-winning assist against Ipswich.
That made it four league victories from their last five matches for Roberto De Zerbi’s side and the Italian could only have enjoyed the view from the stands as he served his one-match touchline ban. Tottenham have struggled to match their London rivals Arsenal and Chelsea’s record of producing homegrown players in recent years but they appear to have struck gold with Williams-Barnett.
Harry Winks was the last academy graduate to score on his debut more than a decade ago – a feat that Kane also achieved two years earlier against Sunderland. Yet after Spurs decided to allow the England Under-21s striker Will Lankshear to join Middlesbrough in the summer, there was no chance that Williams-Barnett would be allowed to follow him out of the door. He became the 900th player ever to represent Spurs when he made his debut last year and the teenager left the field here to a standing ovation that he will never forget.
“I told him to play like he plays in the park with his friends, with the same freedom,” said De Zerbi. “And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembélé, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal. Luca is a special player. I’m not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He’s very young but at same time he’s very mature. He is older than his age.”
Asked whether his protege has the potential to be compared to the Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal, De Zerbi added: “Yes, I think so. One of the best things in my career I’ve seen today on the bus to the stadium. He was watching [clips] on YouTube of Ronaldinho, Hazard. I think he’s a special guy, because if one hour before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. Having the qualities is one thing but he has the passion for football, too.”
After a promising start to the campaign, Ipswich’s momentum has stalled – they have now gone five games without a victory. But Gary O’Neil, who has already seen 16-year-old Max Dowman score twice for Arsenal against his side in the Carabao Cup, acknowledged that they had been second best throughout. “You need things to be perfect when we come to a place like this and we didn’t make things easy for ourselves,” he said.
De Zerbi dropped a huge hint that Williams-Barnett could be handed his opportunity to start after two impressive cameos against Crystal Palace and Leeds. “Maybe, maybe,” he said on Friday. It turned out that the decision was actually taken last week, although the absence of Sandro Tonali due to illness forced Spurs into a reshuffle in midfield as Mateus Fernandes was handed the holding role.
Solanke has struggled to fill the void left by Kane since joining from Bournemouth in 2024 but looked in determined mood and he was inches wide with a swivel and shot from inside the area. A driving run from Williams-Barnett had the home supporters off their feet, with Solanke again going close from the resulting corner. It then needed a timely block from the teenager to stop Ipswich breaking downfield.
His big moment arrived less than 60 seconds later. Porro’s ball to the back post should have been dealt with by Abdoul Ouattara, only for a moment’s hesitation to allow Williams-Barnett to muscle in front of him and apply the finish with his knee. “He’s one of our own,” sang the Tottenham fans in delight.
Mohammed Kudus was unfortunate to see his superb effort from a free-kick cannon off the inside of the post and away to safety. Williams-Barnett will be disappointed not to have scored his second when he miskicked inside the six-yard box with the goal gaping. James Maddison was then denied by a brilliant save from Christian Walton and Williams-Barnett left the field at half-time looking very pleased with himself as he waved to his family in the crowd.
His smile grew even broader after Darnell Furlong was left bamboozled by a direct run down the left flank before the youngster delivered the ball on a plate for Solanke to score his first goal here since March. The defeat could have been worse for Ipswich had it not been for Walton, and O’Neil will know they are in danger of being sucked into trouble if this winless run continues. There are no such concerns for Tottenham these days. Thanks to Williams-Barnett, their future looks much brighter than a few weeks ago.

Leeds dominate Chelsea for first Stamford Bridge win since 1999
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is already in firefighting mode.
His team were booed by their own supporters at several points during a dominant 4-1 Leeds victory at Stamford Bridge, their first win there since 1999.
The first negative reaction came at half-time while the score was still 1-1. The ground then began to empty after the third and fourth Leeds goals, and the fans remaining voiced their dissent once more at the final whistle.
Although there were mitigating circumstances, including a potentially harsh penalty decision against them and the loss of midfielder Moises Caicedo to injury, joining a five-strong list of players on the treatment table, the defeat was thoroughly deserved.
It leaves Chelsea with three losses in their past four Premier League matches and they have slipped from fifth place to eighth, already 14 points behind league leaders Arsenal .
In October, Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the Premier League era, while the 1-0 defeat at bottom club Sunderland before the international break was another alarm bell.
It is the first time since 1967 that Chelsea have lost at home to both Leeds and Spurs in the same season.
"We need to find solutions, for sure, because there will be setbacks during any game," Alonso said after the match.
"To be able to go through that and to know that it's still so long to play, it's something mandatory in this competition and today I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment mentally.
'Officials can't use common sense' - was Rogers handball correct?
Indeed, even when Chelsea have been winning matches, they have often looked unconvincing.
Yet Blues supporters chanted their new manager's name and seemed optimistic after the summer transfer business - despite a disappointing 10th-place finish last season.
Club record £117m signing Morgan Rogers was joined by the experienced trio of Emiliano Martinez, Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.
It was the clinical finishing of Rogers, along with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro earlier in the season, that masked the underlying fragility of Alonso's team.
Before this weekend, the Blues ranked 14th for expected goal difference and were joint 12th in Opta's expected points table.
After their latest setback, ex-England forward and BBC Match of the Day pundit Alan Shearer said: " Chelsea were all over the place. Once Moises Caicedo went off injured early on, there was no physicality and they looked weak.
"They hardly created anything going forward and the back four didn't look comfortable. There was no desire, cohesion or fight from the home side, but we shouldn't take anything away from Leeds .
"Two weeks ago Chelsea were bullied by Sunderland centre-forward Brian Brobbey and they let Dominic Calvert-Lewin do the same today, which is alarming.
"It's fair to say Xabi Alonso's honeymoon period is over. He needs to tell his players this simply isn't good enough. They are miles off it and have to do better in every department."
Xabi Alonso was appointed Chelsea manager on a four-year deal in May
In Alonso's defence, Chelsea had problems before his arrival.
They finished 10th last season, having been outrun in 37 of their 38 matches, and had three managers during a chaotic campaign.
Remarkably, Chelsea have seven more points from corresponding fixtures this season and last, but it mostly serves to show how low the bar was set.
Champions League qualification was again the club's pre-season target and Alonso's appointment was designed to bring stability and authority.
The former Real Madrid and Liverpool midfielder had an impressive playing career and earned much early admiration as a manager, guiding Bayer Leverkusen to a league and cup double in 2024.
However, the Spaniard, who was sacked by Real Madrid last season, has yet to establish any real consistency - beyond his defence leaking goals regularly.
Only Crystal Palace , Coventry City and Ipswich Town have conceded more goals than Chelsea this season.
Chelsea are also now averaging fewer than a goal per game since Joao Pedro suffered a thigh injury in training. Alongside Pedro and now Caicedo, Jorrel Hato, Maxence Lacroix, Reece James and Jamie Gittens are also injured.
It highlights how they have gained little benefit of having a season without European football.
Alonso is also beginning to face criticism from sections of the fanbase for both his team selections and substitutions.
Chief among the reasons is the constant chopping and changing of the starting XI, having now made 28 line-up changes (behind only Tottenham ) while also switching between back-four and back-three systems.
In addition, Alonso is being criticised for his use of personnel, having deployed Pedro Neto as a striker on two occasions and, some would argue, not made enough use of exciting young winger Estevao.
Against Leeds he gave striker Emmanuel Emegha his first start alongside Estevao and, although the Dutch striker scored, the pair were the first players he substituted while Chelsea were chasing the game at 3-1 down.
Similarly, his late in-game interventions are under scrutiny, including the decision to bring on striker Welbeck only in the 90th minute of the defeat by Spurs .
He took until the 64th minute to make changes against Leeds when Chelsea were already 3-1 down. Only three clubs had made more substitutions in the last 15 minutes than Chelsea in the league this season.
Given Leeds ' strengths, Chelsea should have been better prepared for what was coming. Before kick-off, Leeds had applied more high-intensity pressures in the opposition half than any other team in the Premier League.
They had also generated the most expected goals from set-pieces and won the most duels. Leeds maintained those trends at Stamford Bridge against a Chelsea side often accused of being soft.
Chelsea have had problems in recent seasons, but this was still their worst home defeat since a 4-1 loss to Brentford in 2022.
Likewise, it is almost uncharted territory in Alonso's managerial career, having only previously lost at home by a three-goal margin once.
Players displayed negative body language and argued with one another both during the match and after the final whistle.
As a result, Alonso has gone from needing to fix defensive issues to dealing with problems that appear to be spreading throughout the squad.

Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United , who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.
It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.
Farke’s side were tactically superior against flimsy opposition. For Chelsea, who were jeered off after their fifth defeat in 11 games, the indignities piled high. Records are falling, but not in a good way. This is the first time in 67 years they have lost grudge matches at home to Leeds and Tottenham in the same season, leaving Alonso on shaky ground with supporters, and there was further alarm when Cole Palmer appeared to clash with Willie Isa after the side’s “cultural architect” urged Chelsea’s No 10 to acknowledge the crowd at full-time.
Palmer cut a disgruntled figure throughout and did nothing to make Thomas Tuchel rethink his decision to leave him out of the England squad. The one mitigating factor is that few players will thrive in a directionless team. What does Alonso want Chelsea to be? No one knows. There are no patterns of play and the main takeaway from this surrender is that the only sign of an identity was an addiction to calamitous defending.
Calvert-Lewin followed the lead of Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey by tormenting Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana. Alonso was appointed in the summer but the pressure is mounting already. The Spaniard’s control even let him down when a ball dropped towards the technical area in the second half.
It was some turnaround from the visitors, who trailed when Emmanuel Emegha marked his full debut by scoring his first goal since joining Chelsea from Strasbourg last summer. Farke continues to excel. The best that can be said of Alonso is that he needs time. Losing Moisés Caicedo early on was a blow. Even then it is impossible to understand Alonso’s intended style of play. There is an emptiness to Chelsea. They faced 21 shots and failed to up the physicality after crumbling against Sunderland.
Admittedly Alonso is dealing with João Pedro’s absence in attack. He has toyed with a false nine in recent weeks, but used a target man this time and the early signs were promising. Emegha gave Chelsea a focal point and finished well when an error from James Justin allowed Rogers to send the striker through on goal.
Leeds were on top when they conceded. Chelsea had lost Caicedo, who made way for Jordan Henderson after injuring his back in a collision with Justin, and were already wobbling. Calvert-Lewin spurned three excellent headed chances and Leeds levelled after 28 minutes.
Chelsea had no defensive leaders. Fofana is too easily ruffled in the air and was involved in the equaliser. He sent a routine header back into dangerous territory and Chelsea panicked. Josh Acheampong mistimed his jump as the ball bounced around and Calvert-Lewin was able to find Okafor, who cut inside and slipped a low shot past Emiliano Martínez.
Farke was rightly disappointed that Leeds were not ahead at half-time. Tarik Muharemovic charged forward from defence, away from Palmer’s feeble challenge, and crossed for Calvert-Lewin to flick wide. Ethan Ampadu ran midfield, outshining Henderson and Romeo Lavia, and the Leeds wing-backs were wonderful. Ao Tanaka went close and Muharemovic grimaced after having a goal disallowed for offside.
Alonso looked bewildered. Colwill, low on confidence since returning from a knee injury, kept misplacing simple passes and Estêvão Willian was ineffective on the right. Chelsea were jeered off and made a dreadful start to the second half. Martínez should have conceded a penalty for a challenge on Calvert-Lewin. Michael Oliver then pointed to the spot when Rogers was adjudged to have handled Jayden Bogle’s shot.
• Leeds have won their first game against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge in all competitions since December 1999, ending a run of 10 away games against the Blues without victory (D2 L8), while they’ve scored 4+ goals away at Chelsea for the first time since January 1970 (5-2).
• Leeds have won their first Premier League game in London since May 2022 (2-1 against Brentford), ending a run of 15 matches in the Capital without victory (D4 L11), while it’s their biggest winning margin in London since April 2003 (6-1 against Charlton).
• Leeds’ Ao Tanaka (pictured with Cole Palmer) committed three fouls inside the first six minutes against Chelsea; no player has ever fouled more often inside six minutes in a Premier League game on record (since 2003-04). Opta
It looked harsh given Rogers’ arm was close to his body and the ball hit him close to the shoulder but the decision was upheld after a VAR check. Calvert-Lewin stepped up to score and the result was never in doubt once Leeds led. Chelsea, who were mentally fragile, crumbled. Leeds were rampant. Chelsea could not cope with Ampadu’s long throws. One was half cleared but Sean Longstaff worked the ball back to Ampadu, who crossed for Okafor to make it 3-1.
“We are in a fragile moment mentally,” Alonso said. “When we receive a punch we didn’t recover. The fans were disappointed because the expectations are high. I understand their disappointment. There were moments that we were not competing at the level required.”
The closing stages were miserable for Chelsea, who have already conceded 20 goals. Leeds cruised and completed the humiliation when Aaronson, a late substitute, turned past Malo Gusto before sliding a shot through Martínez’s grasp.
The home sections had already emptied out. Those who stayed soon made their displeasure clear.

Report and free match highlights as Aston Villa held to frustrating draw against Sunderland at Villa Park; Leon Goretzka and Emi Buendia had half-chances but Villa created very little; Chemsdine Talbi almost snatched late winner for visitors, who remain in Premier League bottom three
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Aston Villa were held to a frustrating 0-0 draw against Sunderland as Regis Le Bris' side soaked up the pressure to secure a point away at Villa Park.
Unai Emery's side had 72 per cent possession but failed to make their dominance on the ball count with an expected goals value of just 0.98 xG accumulated.
Opportunities to break the deadlock within the tepid performance were limited to half-chances through Emi Buendia's attempted chip in the first half and Leon Goretzka's shot, which was skewed wide from close range.
Captain John McGinn, who was a shock omission from the starting line-up, sparked a degree of urgency with his introduction at the hour mark and orchestrated the only real goalscoring chance for his side.
The midfielder pulled the ball across the face of goal but substitute Brian Madjo, 17, who had replaced Nicolas Jackson moments earlier, was nowhere to be seen to tap it home.
Sunderland came close to snatching a late winner when Chemsdine Talbi flooded forward on the counter but curled his ambitious shot just wide of the target, to the delight of Zion Suzuki, who was scrambling to meet it.
The point momentarily lifts the Black Cats above Manchester United into 18th, although they remain in the bottom three on goal difference.
For Villa, it was another afternoon to forget as they failed to get back to winning ways after previously squandering a two-goal lead on two occasions at Old Trafford last time out. They sit outside of the top 10 and are winless in their last
"A little bit frustrated, but how we are building our team and recovering our confidence in our style of playing, today was a step forward.
"We were dominating, we were progressing with passes and we were in a good position to control the game, but we didn't create many clear chances.
"Today is not enough, but we know how we have to try and build the team and how we can feel better. One step forward, clear in the style. Keep going forward."
"A good point on the road, absolutely, against a strong opponent. They have many threats everywhere on the pitch, well organised, well coached, good dynamic.
"It was crucial to be solid out of possession, to be able to protect our goal and to manage different threats. In 1v1s, they are so skilled; they can combine in tight areas as well, so the shape we used today was crucial.
"We are a little bit frustrated [with on the ball play] because you have to exploit the opportunities you have but it's just a question of time and confidence.
"Obviously, from the start of the season it was important to switch a little bit. Now we are in the fight really clearly and we have a clear strategy to handle the situation.
"After Chelsea, was it an accident? The answer is no, because we can repeat against another opponent.
"After that, it's a question of just adjusting in transition, the decision-making, the accuracy of the last pass or the last decision. It's a question of time."
The last time these two sides met at Villa Park, it was a seven-goal thriller which included two goals within the final five minutes of regular time and a stoppage-time winner from Tammy Abraham.
This game was the direct antithesis of that game. I have rarely covered a match when absolutely nothing happened but this is one of them.
Sunderland's game plan worked to perfection. They invited the pressure from Villa, denied the likes of Jackson and Manzambi the space they thrive in, and waited for a rare chance to counter. Which almost paid off when Talbi raced forward late on.
Villa lacked a spark throughout this game, which nearly arrived with McGinn's introduction, but when that ball fizzed across the face of goal without a claret and blue shirt to tap it home, Unai Emery likely knew what kind of afternoon it was for his side.
Sunderland secure a point, another building block after their poor start, while Villa will now be tasked with finding that elusive creative spark ahead of their trip to Galatasaray in midweek. There are better atmospheres to try and do that in.

Sihirli Annem 'in unutulmaz çocuk karakterlerinden Buket'e hayat veren Şara Türesel, yıllar içindeki değişimi ve yeni hayatıyla dikkat çekti. Ekranlardan uzaklaşan eski oyuncu, dizideki arkadaşlarıyla neden görüşmediğini de anlattı.
Türk televizyonlarının unutulmaz yapımlarından Sihirli Annem , yıllar geçmesine rağmen karakterleriyle hatırlanmaya devam ediyor. Dizinin çocuk oyuncuları arasında yer alan Şara Türesel de canlandırdığı Buket karakteriyle hafızalara kazındı. Çilek'in en yakın arkadaşlarından biri olan Buket, aynı zamanda Çilek ve Kaan'ın sınıf arkadaşıydı. Yuvarlak gözlükleri, okul forması ve kendine özgü tavırlarıyla dizinin dikkat çeken karakterleri arasında yer aldı. Perilerin ve sihirli dünyanın varlığını öğrenen az sayıdaki kişiden biri olan Buket, zaman zaman Çilek'in yaptığı sihirlere de tanıklık ediyordu. Çocukça kıskançlıkları ve inatçı tavırlarıyla izleyicinin tanıdığı karakter, Şara Türesel'in oyunculuk kariyerindeki en bilinen rollerinden biri oldu.
Sihirli Annem 'in ardından oyunculuk kariyerine devam etmeyen Şara Türesel, eğitimine ağırlık verdi. Yeditepe Üniversitesi Radyo, Televizyon ve Sinema Bölümü'nden mezun olan Türesel, kariyerini farklı bir yönde sürdürmeyi tercih etti. Ekranlardan uzaklaşmasına rağmen müziğe olan ilgisini kaybetmedi. Bir dönem Benimle Söyle yarışmasına katılarak jüri karşısında şarkı söyledi. Daha sonra Türkiye'den ayrılan eski oyuncu, yaşamını yurt dışında sürdürmeye başladı.
Şara Türesel, Türkiye'den ayrıldıktan sonra Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'ne yerleşti. Kaliforniya eyaletinin San Diego kentinde yaşamaya başlayan Türesel, burada evlenerek kendisine yeni bir hayat kurdu. Dört yıldır San Diego'da yaşadığını belirten eski oyuncu, artık televizyon projeleri yerine günlük yaşamına odaklanıyor. Çocukluk yıllarında Sihirli Annem 'de izleyici karşısına çıkan Türesel'in bugünkü görünümü de yıllar içindeki değişimini ortaya koydu.
Şara Türesel, takipçilerinden gelen soruları yanıtlarken Sihirli Annem ekibiyle ilişkisine dair dikkat çekici açıklamalarda bulundu. Bir takipçisinin "Sihirli Annem ekibinden görüştüğün kişiler var mı?" sorusuna eski oyuncu şu yanıtı verdi: "Diziden kimseyle görüşmüyorum."
Sihirli Annem'in set günlerini de hatırlayan Şara Türesel, o dönemde genellikle kendi halinde vakit geçirdiğini söyledi. Set aralarında kitap okuduğunu ve müzik dinlediğini belirten Türesel, diğer oyuncularla sohbet etmesine rağmen aralarında güçlü bir arkadaşlık bağı oluşmadığını ifade etti. Eski oyuncu, o günlere ilişkin şu sözleri kullandı: "2012 yılındaki sette kimseyle bir bağ kuramadığımı hatırlıyorum. Sette de ben genelde kitap okuyup müzik dinliyordum. Tabii ki sohbet ediyordum ama çok büyük bir yakınlık kuramadığımı hatırlıyorum. Setten mi kaynaklıydı yoksa herkes herkesle mi aynıydı, onu hatırlayamıyorum."

For Aston Villa , a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago.
Villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely.
“I am trying to select the players I think that are ready to play and the selection is thinking for the best of the team,” said Emery, who was again reluctant to blame the empty North Stand as a factor behind their disappointing home form, a sharp contrast to their 11-game winning run here last season. “In my experiences here and in Spain, when they [stadiums] are in works like we are in now, it’s a small sacrifice, but it’s not an excuse,” Villa’s manager added. “We have to play with this situation and next year it will be better.”
Villa’s frustration was underlined by a moment on the verge of half-time, when Emery gave Sunderland’s kit man, Luke Purcell, a gentle shove on the sidelines in an attempt to speed up a Villa restart. “We have increased our demands a lot, our level, but still there are favourites in front of us, to reach the top six, top four,” Emery said. “We are now again in a new construction with some new players who are sharing their qualities and we are trying to mix different players, young players to build our structure as fast as possible.”
With 90 minutes and 25 seconds showing on the big screens, Chemsdine Talbi almost snatched victory for Sunderland , the Moroccan winger shaving the upright of Zion Suzuki’s goal with a spell-bending strike. Talbi did almost everything right, bursting past Aaron Wan-Bissaka, comfortably eliminating the defender, before using Boubacar Kamara as a mannequin to get his bearings, but his curling right-foot shot was ultimately a few inches too close to the post. For Villa, a first clean sheet in the league here since March, but this draw extended their winless run to five matches in all competitions.
For Sunderland, this may not have been the dopamine hit of beating Chelsea, but it was was another gutsy showing, and without two key players in Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey, both of whom were absent through injury. It was a big team performance, another feather in the cap of Jules Ahoka, the 20-year-old midfielder who shone on his first Premier League start. Ahoka started last season playing on sandy pitches in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s second division. “He is getting better game after game,” Le Bris said.
Sunderland were happy to soak up the Villa pressure. Emery introduced the 17-year-old Brian Madjo, who trained with England under-21s during the international break, but in place of Nicolas Jackson rather than to join him in attack. By which point Mbaye had entered and combined with McGinn to fashion another nearly moment. Disbelief reigned in the stands, but had Talbi located the top corner, things could have felt a lot worse at the final whistle.

Khiara Keating’s resilient performance in goal denied Chelsea, the Women’s Super League leaders, and earned Liverpool a point. After hard-fought 1-0 wins against Manchester City last Saturday and Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday night, Chelsea drew a blank.
Against Gareth Taylor’s side, Chelsea’s lack of cutting edge was clear a week after beating City to go top. The calf injury picked up by Melvine Malard against City, the absence of Lauren James, who has a thigh injury, and the form of Aggie Beever-Jones, who scored her first WSL goal in more than a year in the 6-0 defeat of Charlton, have left Chelsea’s attack short.
Despite almost 70% possession and 47 touches in the box to Liverpool’s 12, Sonia Bompastor’s side amassed only 19 shots to Liverpool’s 13 and seven on target to their opponents’ four. Although the Blues remain unbeaten in the WSL, their third draw in five games in all competitions means City can leapfrog them at the top if they beat Tottenham on Sunday.
Liverpool had chances, particularly in the first half, but were hanging on after the break and Keating helped them to a fourth clean sheet, a tally bettered only by Bompastor’s side.
“It was a bit stressful; we don’t want to sit back but in games like this you have ‌to ride it out,” Keating told Sky Sports. “A clean sheet is ​always on our minds every game. We knew the mission. It was such a close game, it could have gone either way.”
The January transfer window will give the Blues an opportunity to strengthen their attack, but with three games before the winter break they need to step up in the final third, starting with their tricky fixture against London City Lionesses on 12 December after the international break.

Report as Celtic beat St Mirren 4-1; Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain opened the scoring; Camilo Duran and Luke McCowan made it three before the break; Callum McGregor fired in a fourth for Celtic; Killian Phillips pulled a goal back from the penalty spot
Celtic looked refreshed after the international break as they eased to a 4-1 win against St Mirren.
Injuries meant Alex Oxlade-Camberlain and Luke McCowan were drafted into the starting XI and both scored in a dominant performance at Celtic Park.
Camilo Duran scored in between the above pair after he had two early finishes ruled out for offside.
McGregor added a fourth with a low strike into the bottom corner from the edge of the box.
Celtic's perfect afternoon came undone when Sam Johnstone caught Calvin Ramsay inside the box, and Killian Phillips scored from the penalty spot.
Martin O'Neill also introduced former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joel van den Berg for a debut in the second half and the 19-year-old showed some good touches.
Celtic are seven points clear of Rangers before their trip to Motherwell later on Saturday, live on Sky Sports . St Mirren are ninth, one point above the Steelmen.

The recalled midfielders Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan both scored as Celtic beat St Mirren 4-1. The champions brushed off the loss of midfield pair Mika Baur and Benjamin Nygren to injury to consolidate their place at the top of the Premiership.
The centre-forward Camilo Duran was also on target as Celtic killed the game late in the first half with three goals in nine minutes. Callum McGregor grabbed his first league goal of the season before Killian Phillips scored a consolation from the spot.
With Baur facing up to 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Nygren nursing a heel problem, Martin O’Neill would have been delighted with how his midfield functioned.
Oxlade-Chamberlain made his fifth start of the season and McCowan his second. The pair had never started a game together before. O’Neill also introduced the former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joël van den Berg for a debut in the second half and the 19-year-old showed some good touches.
Celtic started with a new-look front three of Duran flanked by Jota and Yang Hyun-jun. Duran was a constant threat and had two goals disallowed for offside in the opening quarter.
Yang was instrumental in the 33rd-minute opener, racing past Declan John and drilling a low pass which ultimately fell for Oxlade-Chamberlain to stroke into the bottom corner.
The South Korean soon passed up a brilliant chance, opting to look for Duran when played clean through by the goalkeeper Sam Johnstone. The pass was under-hit and Alex Gogic cleared.
Duran was on the end of a far better ball in the 40th minute, cushioning home a volley after a superb whipped cross by Kieran Tierney. Duran soon set up Jota, who was denied by Jacob Chapman, before finding Tierney, who provided another assist as McCowan drilled a first-time finish.
Celtic went four ahead in the 63rd minute when the ball broke for McGregor on the edge of the box. The captain quickly shifted the ball on to his right foot and swept it into the bottom corner.
Johnstone blew his chance of a clean sheet when he crashed into Calvin Ramsay as he came off his line to punch the ball. Phillips converted the resulting 70th-minute penalty and St Mirren kept pushing with Johnstone saving well from Ismeal Kabia and Samuel Ramos coming close.
Hearts returned to winning ways in spectacular style as they destroyed 10-man Dundee 8-0. They went into the game on the back of a run of three straight defeats but they ran riot, scoring four in the first half thanks to Sabah Kerjota, a Pierre Landry Kaboré double and an own goal by Ryan Finnigan.
Dundee were reduced to 10 men after the break with Owen Bevan shown a straight red card before Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Kerjota with his second and Stuart Findlay blew Dundee away with four more goals.
Mario Frick enjoyed a dream start to life as Aberdeen manager by edging a six-goal thriller with a 4-2 win at Kilmarnock . Kevin Nisbet’s double along with Brad Lyons and Findlay Marshall strikes secured three priceless points to leave the Rugby Park side rooted to the bottom
The visitors climbed to eighth spot after a remarkable afternoon where the Pittodrie side hit a much-needed scoring streak. Aberdeen opted to dispense with the services of Stephen Robinson after a run of one win from seven which saw them sink to second bottom and Frick was appointed as his replacement last Sunday.
Dundee United recorded their biggest ever win at Easter Road with an impressive 4-0 thrashing of Hibernian . Zac Sapsford’s first-half double laid the foundations before Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall found the net after the break.
The visitors were well worth the three points as they cemented their place in the top six and picked up their first win in Leith since 2021. It was a humbling afternoon for Hibs, who thought they had turned a corner under their new head coach, Marink Reedijk, after back-to-back victories before the international break.
Falkirk clung on to clock up six top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1966 with a 2-1 home victory against St Johnstone . John McGlynn’s team scored early in each half to remain third.
Jacob Murrell’s eighth goal of a superb debut season sent Falkirk on their way inside six minutes. Finley Barbrook’s second goal in as many games on 48 minutes doubled the advantage. Josh Campbell nodded in a late reply to serve up a scare but the hosts held firm.

Report and free match highlights as Leeds beat Chelsea in the Premier League; Noah Okafor scored twice after Emmanuel Emegha had given hosts lead; Dominic Calvert-Lewin put Leeds ahead with a penalty; Brenden Aaronson capped Leeds' first victory at Stamford Bridge since 1999
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Leeds dismantled Chelsea and increased the pressure on manager Xabi Alonso with an outstanding performance in a stunning 4-1 win.
Chelsea were booed off at half-time and full-time after suffering their third Premier League defeat in four games, a run which has seen them slip to eighth, as Leeds earned their first victory at Stamford Bridge since 1999.
Alonso's side have also been dumped out of the Carabao Cup and are already without European football this season.
Emmanuel Emegha gave the hosts a first-half lead on his first start, but Noah Okafor deservedly equalised before half-time, and Leeds ran riot after the break. Dominic Calvert-Lewin put the visitors ahead with a penalty, Okafor smashed in his second and Brenden Aaronson capped an outstanding away win to move Leeds sixth.
Four of Chelsea's five league defeats have now come without the injured Joao Pedro with his absence felt again despite Emegha smashing in the opener. The 23-year-old, making only his third appearance, caught James Trafford out at his near post although the striker was starved of service.
His goal came after Moises Caicedo was forced off following a heavy fall, and against the run of play after Calvert-Lewin had sent a header against the crossbar, but Leeds equalised within three minutes.
Calvert-Lewin slipped in Okafor, who with three Chelsea defenders around him in the box still managed to send a low, left-footed shot through the legs of Levi Colwill, across Emi Martínez and into the bottom right corner.
From there, Leeds were dominant until the end. Calvert-Lewin flicked a shot just wide, had a header saved, and Tarik Muharemovic's goal was ruled out for offside, all before half-time. Chelsea got worse still after the break.
Martinez's return in goal did little to settle a shaky defence, which was under pressure right from the restart, before Jayden Bogle's rocket struck the right arm of Morgan Rogers and referee Michael Oliver pointed to the spot. Calvert-Lewin sent Martinez the wrong way after VAR had backed the on-field decision following a lengthy check.
Chelsea never once looked like being able to recover and Leeds soon added a third. Ethan Ampadu's low cross from the right deflected up into the middle, and Okafor slammed a close-range volley into the top-left corner in the 58th minute.
It was too soon for the home fans to head for the exits, but they groaned every time Chelsea lost the ball, and a few boos followed Alonso's substitutions before they left en masse when Aaronson tucked in a fourth in added time.
"After the equaliser, after the change [Caicedo], we lost the momentum completely. Until then, we were doing okay. We were creating, we were coming out from the pressure, but from that moment they started believing and we started not believing and it changed totally.
"And after that, we never got the good feeling mentality at any moment, and we were not able to cope with the pressure, and we didn't get close to the goal, so it completely changed it.
"We need to find solutions for sure because there will be setbacks during any game and to be tougher and to be able to go through that and to know that it's still so long to play, it's something mandatory in this competition.
"Today I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment mentally, confidence, when we receive a punch that we don't recover that strong, that tough enough."
"I expected Chelsea to come out with a bit more oomph in the second half. But our intensity and the way that we played and the way that we set up against them, they couldn't handle it. That reflected in the scoreline."
"Great performance. I would have been disappointed with a draw today. I was a bit disappointed even at half-time when it was just a draw because from the first to the last [minute], we were the better side.
"We dominated this game, made sure that our plan for this game worked. We wanted to play on the front foot; we wanted to press Chelsea high; we wanted to make sure that they couldn't show their world-class potential.
"I still think that Chelsea came out motivated today and also played with intensity. I just checked the physical data, they were there with higher physical intensity than in their last games, but we still have outperformed them.
"It's important in this period of the season to collect points. It gives us more confidence but we travelled here with confidence and belief that it would be possible to give such a dominant performance.
"I can't wait to be on the sofa with coffee and cake and to watch this game back."

Ukrayna Ligi'nde sezonun 13. hafta maçında Arda Turan yönetimindeki Shakhtar Donetsk, evinde Livyi Bereh ile karşı karşıya geldi. Rakibiyle 1-1 berabere kalan Shakhtar sürpriz bir puan kaybı yaşadı.
Livyi Bereh, 19. dakikada Nazarii Vorobchak'la öne geçti. İlk devre konuk takımın üstünlüğüyle tamamlanırken Shakhtar Donetsk beraberlik golünü 61'de Alisson Santana ile buldu. Karşılaşmanın kalan dakikalarında skor değişmedi ve 90 dakika 1-1'lik beraberlik sonuçlandı.
Ligde ilk sırada yer alan Shahktar Donetsk 30, 11. basamaktaki Livyi Bereh ise 10 puana yükseldi. Karşılaşmanın ardından Shakhtar Donetsk Teknik Direktörü Arda Turan açıklamalarda bulundu.
Arda Turan takımın performansını eleştirirken şunları söyledi:
"İlk yarıdan sonra 10 oyuncunun tamamını değiştiremediğim için dört oyuncu değiştirdim. Şimdi tam olarak neyin yanlış gittiğini ve hazırlıkta nerede hata yaptığımı bulmam gerekiyor. Bugünkü maçın, bir buçuk yıldır antrenman yaptığımız ve bu sayede olumlu sonuçlar ve zaferler elde ettiğimiz oyun tarzından çok uzak olduğunu vurgulayabilirim. Bağlamı dikkate almalısınız. Çok fazla süre alamayan futbolcu vardı, bu yüzden muhtemelen konsantrasyon eksikliği yaşadılar ve bu da oyun standartlarımıza uymalarını engelledi. Rakip sahanın son yaratıcılıktan uzak kaldık ve çok aceleci kararlar aldık. Çok üzgünüz ve şimdi zorlu ve önemli bir işimiz var."
“Bu karşılaşmayı bana bir buçuk yıl önce sorsaydınız, çok daha olumlu olurdum, ama şimdi gerçekler değişti. Bir ay önce bile daha iyi olduğumuzu söylerdim ama şimdi Fenerbahçe'nin yeni bir teknik direktörü var, onun liderliğinde çok iyi başladılar ve ilerlemeye devam ediyorlar. Favori Fenerbahçe."
"Bugün sahada bir sürü başarısız karar varsa, öncelikle herkesin kendini sorgulaması gerektiğini vurgulamak isterim. Kulüp, kendimiz ve federasyon olarak Ukrayna için tarihi bir deneyim kazanma fırsatımız var. Elbette zor olacak ve bir anlamda sahada acı çekmek zorunda kalacağız ancak bu yolculuk boyunca bizi başarıya götüren önemli özellikleri hatırlamalıyız.”
Maça ilişkin ayrıca Arda Turan, " Futbolda duygusuz taktiklerin değersiz olduğunu hatırlamalıyız. Shakhtar, kendi sahasında bugünkü maçta olduğu gibi oynayamaz. Buna asla izin vermeyeceğim. Eğer oyuncular doğru bir şekilde oynamak için konsantrasyon eksikliği yaşadıysa, bu öncelikle benim hatamdır. Bunun sorumluluğunu alacağım ve ne yapabileceğimi anlamak için olabildiğince analiz yapacağım " değerlendirmesinde bulundu.
UEFA Şampiyonlar Ligi'nin 5. haftasında Fenerbahçe, Shakhtar Donetsk ile deplasmanda karşı karşıya gelecek. Shakhtar Donetsk-Fenerbahçe maçı 25 Kasım Çarşamba günü oynanacak ve mücadele TSİ 23.00'te başlayacak.

9. dakikada Gençlerbirliği öne geçti. Kaleci İrfan Can Eğribayat'ın oyuna hızlı soktuğu topu, Oğulcan Ülgün, ara pasıyla defansın arkasına sarkan Traore ile buluşturdu. Traore, kaleciyi çalımladıktan sonra topu ağlara gönderdi: 1-0.
13. dakikada konuk ekibin sağ kanattan atağında Kozlowski'nin ortasında ceza alanında iyi yükselen Halil Dervişoğlu, meşin yuvarlağı kafayla üstten auta yolladı.
16. dakikada Camara'nın soldan ortasında müsait pozisyondaki Maxim'in kafayla vuruşunda top, kaleci İrfan Can Eğribayat'ta kaldı.
35. dakikada Gaziantep FK gole yaklaştı. Halil Dervişoğlu'nun pasıyla ceza sahasında topla buluşan Gidado'nun vuruşunda meşin yuvarlak, direğin dibinden auta gitti.
Karşılaşmanın ilk yarısı, Gençlerbirliği'nin 1-0 üstünlüğüyle tamamlandı.
55. dakikada Traore'nin sağ kanattan ortasında savunmadan dönen topa Tongya vurdu. Mendes, üzerine gelen topu kale önünde ağlara gönderdi ancak VAR incelemesinin ardından gol, ofsayt gerekçesiyle geçersiz sayıldı.
69. dakikada baskı sonucu topu kazanan Salih Uçan, meşin yuvarlağı ceza sahasındaki Gouveia'ya aktardı. Bu futbolcunun şutunda top, savunmadan oyun alanına döndü.
87. dakikada kalecinin önde olduğunu gören Mendes'in orta sahadan şutunda meşin yuvarlak üst ağlarda kaldı.
Öte yandan maçın 71. dakikasında Arda Çağan Çelik ile kafa kafaya çarpışan Abena yerde kaldı. Abena, sağlık görevlilerinin müdahalesinin ardından saha içerisine giren ambulansa taşınarak hastaneye götürüldü.
Türkiye Futbol Federasyonunun kararı doğrultusunda ligde ilk kez bu karşılaşmada "Çoklu Top Sistemi" uygulandı.
Yeni sistemde top toplayıcılar, topu doğrudan futbolculara veremeyecek, yalnızca saha kenarında belirlenmiş alanlarda konumlandırılmış istasyonlara yerleştirmekle sorumlu olacak.
Gaziantep FK'yi 1-0 mağlup eden Gençlerbirliği'nin teknik direktörü Bernd Storck, ligde kalma adına önemli bir galibiyet aldıklarını söyledi.
Storck, Eryaman Stadyumu'ndaki karşılaşmanın ardından düzenlenen basın toplantısında zeminin iki takım için de zorlu olduğunu dile getirdi.
Takımını tebrik ederek sözlerine başlayan Storck, zorlu maçta iyi iş çıkardıklarını belirterek "Bence bu galibiyeti hak ettik. Bir mücadele ruhu ortaya koyduğumuzu düşünüyorum. Beşiktaş maçında iki stoperimizi sakatlıkla ve kırmızı kartla kaybettik. Genç Arda ve Cheikh (Niasse) orta saha oyuncumuz stoperde oynadı. Tongya sağ bekte, yeni bir pozisyonda oynadı. Sakatlığı olmasına rağmen fedakarca o pozisyonda oynadı. Bu 3 puan küme düşme potasından uzaklaşmamız adına çok önemliydi. Bu işi başardığımız için takıma iki gün izin verdim, bu izni hak ettiklerini düşünüyorum." ifadelerini kullandı.
İlk 11'deki savunma dörtlüsünün iyi oynadığını vurgulayan Alman teknik direktör, yarın yapılacak seçimli genel kurula ilişkin, "Arka dörtlümüzün iyi defans yaptıklarını düşünüyorum. Milli aradan dolayı hazırlanmaya da zamanımız oldu. Yeni başkan adayımızın gelmesiyle de bu galibiyetin birleşmesi iyiydi. Dün mevcut başkanımızla beraber, bizimle bir konuşma yaptı. O da bizim açımızdan motive ediciydi. Biz bu takımı ligde tutmak istiyoruz. Bu hedefe maç maç ilerleyeceğiz." değerlendirmesinde bulundu.
Bu zeminde ayakta durmanın zor olduğunu aktaran Storck, "Zemin her iki takım için de zordu ve rakibin pres yapacağını biliyorduk. Oyun olarak durumdan şikayet edemiyorum. Çünkü saha gerçekten çok kötüydü. Oynaması zor bir saha. Bugün gerçekten bu sahada yapılması gereken ne varsa takımım elinden geleni yaptı. En önemlisi 3 puandı." diye konuştu.

Oyuncu Aslıhan Malbora, sevgilisi Çağatay Ulusoy ile önümüzdeki ay yurt dışında nikah kıyacakları yönündeki haberleri yalanladı. İstanbul'da bir tiyatro oyunundan çıkarken gazetecilerin sorularını yanıtlayan Malbora, evlilik iddiası için "Hayır, öyle bir şey yok. Evlenmiyorum" dedi.
Çiftle ilgili son günlerde yalnız düğün değil, bebek iddiaları da gündeme gelmişti. Milliyet muhabiri Mesut Yılmaz'ın sorularını yanıtlayan Malbora'ya, hamilelik iddiaları nedeniyle yasal yola başvurmayı düşünüp düşünmediği soruldu. Oyuncu bu soruya "Hamile değilim, dava açmayı da düşünmüyorum" karşılığını verdi.
Malbora, son dönemde belirgin biçimde kilo veren Çağatay Ulusoy'un zayıflama iğnesi kullandığı yönündeki haberlere de değindi. Sevgilisinin iğne kullanmadığını söyleyen oyuncu, "Hayır, olmadı. Çok disiplinli bir diyet yapıyor" dedi.
Ulusoy da 19 Kasım akşamı Etiler'de Malbora ile birlikte görüntülendiğinde kilo verme sürecine ilişkin soruya "Diyet yaptım" yanıtını vermiş, yeni işinin başladığını ve sabah erken saatlerde sete gideceğini söylemişti.
Aslıhan Malbora, Show TV'de yayımlanan Üç Kuruş dizisinde canlandırdığı Leyla Çaka karakteriyle tanınıyor. Oyuncu, Her Yerde Sen ve Yaban Çiçekleri gibi dizilerde de rol aldı. Malbora ile Medcezir dizisiyle ün kazanan Ulusoy, Netflix dizisi Kübra'da birlikte oynadı; ikilinin ilişkisi Aralık 2024'te basına yansımıştı.
Çiftin önümüzdeki ay yurt dışında evleneceği iddiası son günlerde magazin gündemine taşınmıştı. Malbora'nın tiyatro çıkışındaki sözleri, hem evlilik hem de hamilelik söylentilerine verilen ilk doğrudan yanıt oldu.
Haberler.com'da yer alan yorumlar, kullanıcıların kişisel görüşlerini yansıtır ve haberler.com'un editöryal politikası ile örtüşmeyebilir. Yorumların hukuki sorumluluğu tamamen yazarlarına aittir.
